conceptBreakdown.content:
The **Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion (PIE)** calculates the cardinality of the union of multiple non-disjoint finite sets without overcounting intersections.

### 5.1 PIE Formulations for 2 and 3 Sets

1. **Cardinality of Two Sets**:
   $$\mathbf{|A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B|}$$
   *Corollary (Exact Disjoint Partition)*:
   $$|A \cup B| = |A \setminus B| + |B \setminus A| + |A \cap B|$$

2. **Cardinality of Three Sets**:
   $$\mathbf{|A \cup B \cup C| = |A| + |B| + |C| - |A \cap B| - |B \cap C| - |C \cap A| + |A \cap B \cap C|}$$

3. **Number of Elements in EXACTLY One Set**:
   $$\mathbf{N_{\text{exact1}} = |A| + |B| + |C| - 2(|A \cap B| + |B \cap C| + |C \cap A|) + 3|A \cap B \cap C|}$$

4. **Number of Elements in EXACTLY Two Sets**:
   $$\mathbf{N_{\text{exact2}} = |A \cap B| + |B \cap C| + |C \cap A| - 3|A \cap B \cap C|}$$

5. **Number of Elements in AT LEAST Two Sets**:
   $$\mathbf{N_{\text{atleast2}} = |A \cap B| + |B \cap C| + |C \cap A| - 2|A \cap B \cap C|}$$

### 5.2 Generalization to n Sets (Bonferroni Inequalities)

For finite sets $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$:

$$|\bigcup_{i=1}^n A_i| = \sum_{1 \le i \le n} |A_i| - \sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} |A_i \cap A_j| + \sum_{1 \le i < j < k \le n} |A_i \cap A_j \cap A_k| - \dots + (-1)^{n-1} |A_1 \cap A_2 \cap \dots \cap A_n|$$

Truncating the PIE expansion yields the **Bonferroni Inequalities**:
- **Odd-term truncation** gives an upper bound: $|\bigcup A_i| \le \sum |A_i|$.
- **Even-term truncation** gives a lower bound: $|\bigcup A_i| \ge \sum |A_i| - \sum |A_i \cap A_j|$.
